note: Each figure is the share of reviewed items on which two sources give the same value, with the number of items behind it. First-decision agreement uses the same reference turn; missing mappings are undetermined. Other clock values are the same within the tolerance the selection flags by (a decision time within the agreement settings' decision tolerance, each edge of the prepared window within two seconds; see tolerances); ordinal fields (the codes and items whose codebook entry is ordinal) are compared exactly, and within_one gives beside it the share within one scale point. On a flag-driven sheet the sampled rows are a seeded draw, proportional to each field class's share, from the fields that nothing flagged and whose unit both passes recorded: they are the unbiased estimate of human-model agreement on such fields, not on flagged fields nor on units one pass lacks. On an exchange-level sheet every row is a random draw from the populations the manifest records. The flagged rows were chosen because something looked wrong and understate agreement. human_vs_replicate and primary_vs_replicate cover only the rows that have a replicate value; primary_vs_replicate counts a field once however many coders judged it. unit_presence rows (a turn, exchange or decision only one pass recorded) enter none of these figures; by_field_class.unit_presence gives the share of such units the human judged present, separately for those only the primary and those only the replicate recorded.
